newsitem.title: FRANCE: Fantozzi says budget breakdown before ministers.
newsitem.headline: Fantozzi says budget breakdown before ministers.

text.p: Italy's Foreign Trade Minister Augusto Fantozzi said on Monday the government had drawn up a proposed breakdown between spending and revenue measures in next year's budget but declined to give specific figures.

"The mix has been communicated to ministers but not to the public yet so I can't say (what the figures are)," Fantozzi told a news conference on the sidelines of ministerial talks at the Organisation for Economic Co-Operation and Development.

Italy's government is expected to unveil its rolling three-year economic strategy this week and to outline how the government intends to cut another 25 trillion lire ($15 billion) from the public deficit in next year's budget.

The strategy, known as the economic and financial planning document (DPEF), is due to be approved by the cabinet on Friday and will outline how the government intends to cut another 25 trillion lire ($15 billion) from the public deficit in next year's budget.
"I can't comment on the document which is being discussed. In any discussion consensus will be required between political partners," Fantozzi said.
The DPEF is a crucial part of Italy's plans for stabilising state finances and keeping alive hopes of joining a European currency union by the planned 1999 start date.

Fantozzi had said on Friday that although the government had agreed on the size of budget it was still debating at that stage what the exact mix should be between spending cuts and fresh revenue-raising measures.

Italian newspapers have reported that the government plans to reduce spending by 17 trillion lire -- including eight trillion lire in social security and welfare spending cuts -- and to raise eight trillion lire in increased revenues.
